question: Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index ranked India _______ out of 180 countries, indicating a persistent struggle with public sector corruption.
solution:
The correct answer is 96**__th.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) is a global measure of corruption in the public sector.
 
• In the 2024 CPI, India was ranked 96th out of 180 countries.
 
• This ranking reflects India's ongoing struggle with corruption issues within its public sector.
 
• The CPI score ranges from 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean), and India's score has been relatively stable in recent years.
 
• India's CPI score in 2024 was 38, highlighting the need for continued efforts to combat corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transparency International:**

 
 
• Founded in 1993, it is an international non-governmental organization working to combat global corruption.
 
• It is headquartered in Berlin, Germany, and operates through more than 100 national chapters worldwide.
 
• Transparency International publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index annually.
 
 
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**
 
 
• The CPI is a composite index that ranks countries by their perceived levels of public sector corruption.
 
• It is based on expert assessments and opinion surveys.
 
• The CPI is widely used as a key indicator of corruption globally.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Corruption:**
 
 
• Corruption undermines democracy and the rule of law.
 
• It leads to the misallocation of resources and hampers economic development.
 
• Corruption adversely affects public services and the overall quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Efforts to Combat Corruption in India:**
 
 
• The Indian government has implemented various measures such as the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.
 
• Strengthening of anti-corruption agencies like the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
 
• Introduction of technology-based initiatives like e-governance to reduce corruption.
